The FedHPb model communicates class prototypes between clients and the server, instead of exchanging gradients or model parameters.
FedHPb uses a contrastive supervised loss function to handle class imbalance, without relying on data sampling.
The experiments tested imbalance ratios of 20:1, 50:1, and 100:1 for non-icing to icing samples.
FedHPb outperformed all other methods, achieving average improvements of 19.64% in mF-score and 5.73% in mBalanced Accuracy compared to the second-best method, BiFL.
The testing set had a sample imbalance ratio of 10:1 for non-icing to icing samples.
The main evaluation metrics were F-score (with β=2) and Balanced Accuracy.
Even at the highest imbalance ratio of 100:1, FedHPb maintained high mF-score (73.08%) and mBalanced Accuracy (85.35%).
Methods like BiFL that used a knowledge preservation mechanism may degrade prototype quality and introduce bias if the encoding is not sufficiently refined.
The FedHPb model was evaluated using real data from two wind farms located approximately 700 kilometers apart.
The data from the two wind farms were representative of different climatic conditions, allowing the model to adapt to heterogeneous environments.
The data preprocessing steps included denoising, outlier handling, and missing value imputation to ensure data quality and consistency.
The training set comprised 60% of the data, while the testing set comprised 40%.
The Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimizer was used with a learning rate of 0.01.
The hyper-parameter λ was set to 0.25, and the temperature τ was set to 0.5.
The communication rounds (R) between clients and the server were configured to 20, while the local training epochs (E) were set to 100.
